column2: On the authority of ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb (may Allah be pleased with him), from the Prophet ﷺ, who said: “If you were to rely on Allah as He truly deserves to be relied upon, He would provide for you as He provides for the birds:

they go out in the morning with empty stomachs and return in the evening with full stomachs.” Reported by Imam Aḥmad, al-Tirmidhī, al-Nasāʾī, Ibn Mājah, Ibn Ḥibbān in his Ṣaḥīḥ, and al-Ḥākim; al-Tirmidhī said: “Ḥasan ṣaḥīḥ.”

This hadith is a foundation for reliance on Allah, the Mighty and Majestic (tawakkul), together with taking the lawful means; taking them does not contradict reliance. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ, the master of those who rely [on Allah], entered Makkah in the year of the Conquest wearing a helmet on his head.
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ directed [us] to combine taking the means with dependence on Allah when he ﷺ said in the hadith in Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim (2664):

“Be keen on what benefits you, and seek help from Allah.” This hadith of ʿUmar (may Allah be pleased with him) combines taking the means with reliance on Allah; the taking of means lies in what is mentioned about the birds,

for they go out in the morning khimāṣan, that is, with empty stomachs, seeking provision, and return biṭānan, that is, with full stomachs. Though a person takes the means, he does not depend on them but depends on Allah; nor does he neglect taking the means and then claim that he is relying [on Allah].

Allah has decreed both causes and their effects. Ibn Rajab said in Jāmiʿ al-ʿUlūm wa-l-Ḥikam (2/496–497): “This hadith is a foundation for reliance [on Allah], and shows that it is among the greatest means by which provision is obtained.

Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, said: ‘And whoever fears Allah, He will make for him a way out and provide for him from where he does not expect. And whoever relies upon Allah, then He is sufficient for him’ [al-Ṭalāq 65:2–3]…” He went on to say:

“The reality of reliance is the heart's true dependence on Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, in bringing about benefits and warding off harms in all matters of this world and the Hereafter, entrusting all affairs to Him, and truly believing that none but He gives, withholds, harms or benefits.”
One must rely on Allah and depend on Him to obtain everything sought and ward off everything feared.
One should take the means while relying on Allah; doing so does not contradict reliance.
